notes: kb/Work/PB445.md LANDED. "Data-name-1, data-name-2, identifier-3, or identifier-4 shall not specify a variable-length group" (cite.py --check 14.9.37.3 -> OK, Syntax rules 12). BOTH arms are screened and BOTH are witnessed -- the data-name arm (pb445-search-all-key-variable-length) and the identifier arm (pb445-search-all-sending-variable-length) -- through the ONE VariableLengthCompatibility.IsVariableLength predicate, which already existed and which this rule's absence had left uncalled at this site. THE NOTE'S ORIGINAL SR12 MEASUREMENT WAS A FALSE FINDING and is corrected here: its probe used an OCCURS DEPENDING group as the variable-length witness, but 8.5.1.12.1 defines a variable-length group as "a group item whose data description has at least one dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table as a subordinate item" (cite.py -> OK) -- a dynamic-capacity table is OCCURS DYNAMIC (13.18.38 Format 4), not OCCURS ... DEPENDING ON -- so the clean compile that probe measured was CORRECT and the note also recorded the data-name arm as untested on that basis. Re-witnessed with a genuine variable-length group (a subordinate DYNAMIC LENGTH item, 13.18.19) both arms fire. The rule applies at every edition; the two goldens reject from 2014 because a variable-length group cannot be DECLARED below it, so there is no edition at which either program is accepted. COBOL1965 (key side) and COBOL1966 (sending side).
